The sulfur particles have a median diameter of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers and are mixed with porous carbon by ball milling. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The active material sulfur is combined with porous carbon and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium.

title: Electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell operable at 700 to 850 degrees C and fuel cell system
abstract: This disclosure concerns a tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and a nickel cermet anode. The electrolyte layer is a bilayer of zirconia and ceria with a total thickness of 3 micrometers. The reversible cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 700 to 850 degrees C. The lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte of 98% density blocks gas crossover and raises the open circuit voltage. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate.

title: Surface mount solid electrolytic capacitor and method of reducing leakage current
abstract: Provided is a multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor in which capacitor elements are stacked and connected in parallel. A solid electrolyte of polypyrrole replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. The niobium anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The anode body is a sintered pellet of niobium powder having a specific charge of 50,000 to 150,000 microfarad volts per gram. The hybrid structure improves the self-healing of the dielectric film on the niobium anode. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.3 to 0.55. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A mixed-halide composition containing both chloride and bromide is used so that the lattice is expanded. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The material comprises Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. Specific examples are Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). The Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved ionic conductivity.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a lithium secondary battery using it. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The argyrodite phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. In an embodiment the solid electrolyte layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 and Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or beta-Li3PS4 phase precipitates uniformly. The content of P2O5 is 2 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The glass phase contains P2O5 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with a residual solvent content of 1 wt% or less. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The solid electrolyte obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 1 wt%. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Germanium-substituted perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid stable above 4.5 V and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A halogen-rich argyrodite with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. A halide coating layer may be used together with the ion-conductive solid to improve the cycle life of the all-solid-state battery. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Part of the titanium in the perovskite-type LLTO phase is substituted by germanium in an amount of 5 mol% to 20 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.5 V. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The oxide ion-conductive solid enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a silver-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. The ceramic ion conductor powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LGPS and Li3PS4 material. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The cell shows no short circuit for 1000 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. Suitable compositions include Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The additive comprises silver in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window during fast charging.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a thio-LISICON phase and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a thio-LISICON crystal phase precipitated therein. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or thio-LISICON phase precipitates uniformly. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 260 degrees C, and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm or more. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ceramic ion conductor having a cubic Li6PS5X structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 520 degrees C. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 7.3 mS/cm. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The mixed halogen substitution improves the moisture stability and ionic conductivity of the lithium secondary battery.

title: Core-shell sulfur cathode particles for a lithium-sulfur battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a transition metal sulfide active material that intercalates lithium with a high capacity. A lithium battery comprising the positive electrode and a negative electrode of lithium metal or silicon is also provided. The nickel sulfide is melt-diffused into graphene at 155 degrees C, and the composite contains 60 wt% to 80 wt% of the active material. A solid electrolyte interphase is formed on the lithium metal negative electrode during the first cycles. The method is scalable and compatible with a conventional slurry coating process using polyvinylidene fluoride. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 85%. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The capacity retention after 100 cycles is 85% at 25 degrees C.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide ceramic ion conductor that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns a roll-pressing method for forming a solid electrolyte film without any solvent. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 100 degrees C to form a continuous film. The binder is polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) in an amount of 1.2 wt% to 6 wt%, and the fibrils have an average diameter of 50 nm to 500 nm. The solid electrolyte is preferably beta-Li3PS4. With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 100 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 200 nm to 1000 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. The LLZO, LiF, and Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 500 nm. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. The inorganic layer has a conductivity of 5 x 10^-6 S/cm, and the cell shows a Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% after 100 cycles. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid arsenic-free antimony binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 100 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by uniaxial pressing. The edge sealing portion prevents short circuit and improves the reliability of the cell with a 100 micrometer separator layer. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 300 kPa through an elastic sheet. The restraining member keeps the laminate of 16 cells under pressure for the life of the module. The current collector is a stainless steel foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The module with 16 stacked cells has a voltage of 16 times the cell voltage and an energy density of 350 Wh/L.

title: Tubular solid oxide fuel cell with a nickel cermet anode and a samarium-doped ceria electrolyte
abstract: Described is an electrolyte-supported solid oxide fuel cell with a 15 micrometer thick ceramic electrolyte. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 600 to 750 degrees C. The thin 15 micrometer electrolyte lowers the ohmic resistance and improves the power density of the cell to 0.8 W/cm2. The electrolyte layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a relative density of 96%, and the open circuit voltage is 1.1 V at 600 to 750 degrees C. The cathode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified. The cell can be operated at 600 to 750 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects. The solid electrolyte of samarium-doped ceria is a dense ceramic of 96% density that blocks electrons and gas while conducting oxide ions.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium tungstate coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose Li2WO4 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3InCl6 and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The lithium tungstate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state battery using it. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The precipitated Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved electrochemical window.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The tin substitution amount is 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO, Li7P3S11, and LATP material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.3 mS/cm. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Wet coating method for forming a solid electrolyte layer on a release film and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A method for producing a solid electrolyte sheet by slurry casting, drying, and peeling from a support film is provided. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A solid-state lithium battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The binder is a rubber that keeps the layer flexible after drying and does not block the ion conduction between particles. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the cycle life of the cell.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 72:28 and a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase precipitated therein. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 30% to 65% by X-ray diffraction. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the cycle life and moisture stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium borate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The LiNbO3 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A lithium secondary battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the electrochemical window and interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. The solid electrolyte can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery. The LLZO, Li6PS5Cl, and Li7P3S11 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The solid electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 20 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -20 degrees C. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium sulfide based cathode active material with suppressed polysulfide dissolution
abstract: A positive electrode slurry containing the sulfide active material, ketjen black, and carboxymethyl cellulose is described. The active material molybdenum disulfide is combined with ketjen black and undergoes a conversion or intercalation reaction with lithium. The positive electrode mixture comprises the sulfide active material, a sulfide solid electrolyte of Li6PS5Cl in an amount of 20 wt% to 40 wt%, and carbon, for use in an all-solid-state lithium-sulfur battery. The ketjen black framework keeps the electrode conductive during the volume change of molybdenum disulfide. The positive electrode comprises the composite, a conductive agent, and carboxymethyl cellulose in a weight ratio of 80:10:10. With a sulfur loading of 3 mg/cm2, the areal capacity is 3 mAh/cm2 or more. The confinement of molybdenum disulfide in the ketjen black suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 500 cycles. A lithium secondary battery comprising the positive electrode, a lithium-containing negative electrode, and an electrolyte is also provided.

title: thermally crosslinked polymer electrolyte membrane for a lithium battery and method of preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 60 degrees C. The membrane of 100 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polycarbonate electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 1.0 mS/cm. The membrane further contains a ceramic filler of Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet in an amount of 10 wt% to 30 wt% to form a composite electrolyte. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y) and to a solid-state battery comprising the same. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.12 or less. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 7.3 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte provides improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li3InCl6. The Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. The coating layer has an average thickness of 8 nm and a coverage of 80%, and the interfacial resistance is reduced by 40% relative to uncoated particles. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl, Li2ZrO3, and Li3InCl6 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a solid electrolyte whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in germanium. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide solid electrolyte. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The LLZO, LLTO, and Li2ZrO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity and sinterability.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate and sulfide ion conductor produced thereby
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in ethyl propionate to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the solid-state lithium battery. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium battery is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium zirconate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The all-solid-state lithium battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 350 degrees C. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the solid electrolyte layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 80 mol% or more of the transition metals. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved cycle life and high-voltage stability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an ion-conductive solid whose anodic decomposition at high potential is suppressed by a surface region of 5 nm to 50 nm. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the tin substitution and the surface region. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium scandium chloride solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure
abstract: A rare earth metal halide solid electrolyte with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6. The material comprises Li3InCl6 and Li3YCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the electrochemical window at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A lithium secondary battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region and method for preparing the same
abstract: An air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte in which hydrolysis is suppressed by arsenic-free antimony substitution is provided. The material comprises Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved moisture stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Argyrodite sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed bromine-iodine substitution
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. Partial substitution of bromine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiBr impurity phase. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), Li7P3S11, and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiBr to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 3.5 mS/cm. The ion-conductive solid provides improved cycle life compared with a single-halogen argyrodite of the same halogen content.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is an ion-conductive solid comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 80%. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 60% to 95% by X-ray diffraction. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The ion-conductive solid shows improved ionic conductivity and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ceramic ion conductor particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. The sheet thickness is 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers, the porosity is 30% or less, and the conductivity is 1.4 mS/cm or more. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. The powder is mixed with the PTFE binder at a roll temperature of 80 degrees C to form a continuous film. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A solid-state lithium battery using the sheet shows improved cycle life and a thinner electrolyte layer.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide solid electrolyte obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-SiS2 glass. After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 2.5 mS/cm. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. In an embodiment the material is Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. A dry process in which the solid electrolyte powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is an argyrodite-type ion-conductive solid in which part of the bromine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. A solid-state battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved moisture stability. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite-type phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, bromine, and iodine. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the moisture stability.

title: Halide ion-conductive solid having a close-packed chloride sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the indium in a lithium indium chloride framework. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. In an embodiment the material is lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and HfCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.02 to 0.25. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the electrochemical window.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: A negative electrode structure with a critical current density of 0.7 mA/cm2 or more and a method for suppressing void formation during stripping are provided. The indium additive is dispersed at the interface between the lithium metal layer and the ceramic ion conductor layer by pressing a mixed powder layer. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. A Coulombic efficiency of 98.5% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. Suitable compositions include Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 280 degrees C. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 3.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 50%. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the solid electrolyte. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The LiPON layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 2 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The Li3YCl6 and Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A lithium metal battery using the protective layer shows improved ionic conductivity and Coulombic efficiency.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide solid electrolyte and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 450 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. A solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4 and Li7P3S11, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. The solid electrolyte retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ion-conductive solid sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The sintered body has a relative density of 94%, an average grain size of 8 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. Sintering is performed at 1200 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and LLZO material. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. A lithium excess of 15 mol% is added to the mother powder to compensate the loss of lithium during sintering. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNbO3 shell with high coverage
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and nickel content of 60 mol% or more. The ion-conductive component may be lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and lithium fluoride (LiF). The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the solid-state battery without a drying step. The mixture for the ion-conductive solid is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. Part of the material is a rare earth halide represented by Li3MCl6, wherein M is yttrium, indium, or scandium, prepared by mechanochemical reaction. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 60 mol% or more of the transition metals. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The anion is covalently bonded to the polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The polymer matrix is polyvinylidene fluoride-hexafluoropropylene and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1230 degrees C shows a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm and a relative density of 94%. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 3.2 micrometers to 24 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. Because lithium volatilization is suppressed, the cubic phase is retained and the grain boundary resistance is improved.

title: Pressure jig for a laminated battery cell and method of applying stack pressure of 500 kPa
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a cell structure in which an edge sealing portion prevents short circuit between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The solid electrolyte layer is sandwiched between the lithium iron phosphate positive electrode layer and the negative electrode layer. The unit cells are stacked 4 in series, and the bipolar current collector has the positive electrode on one side and the negative electrode on the other. The cell shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 300 cycles under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The warm isostatic pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The battery is a lithium battery in which the negative electrode layer comprises graphite, silicon, or lithium metal.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. The polymer matrix is polyethylene oxide and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 16:1. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyethylene oxide matrix. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 16:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the polyethylene oxide based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 2.5 MPa to 10 MPa with a lithium fluoride additive. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The ion-conductive solid may comprise Li3YCl6 and lithium fluoride (LiF). The critical current density is 2.1 mA/cm2 or more and the number of cycles without short circuit is 150 cycles or more. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The additive is useful for an anode-free configuration, with improved dendrite suppression.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. An H2S generation of 10 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LATP composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. After ball milling, the ion-conductive solid precursor is pressed and sintered. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The ion-conductive solid may comprise beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In a lithium secondary battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the grain boundary resistance. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 2 hours. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite ion-conductive solid having anion disorder and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite ion-conductive solid whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite phase is 0.05, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11. The halogen-rich composition keeps the argyrodite phase as the main crystal phase and suppresses the precipitation of lithium halide impurity. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and cycle life.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The reaction at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An oxide of the NASICON type such as LATP may be included to widen the electrochemical window at high potential. A superionic argyrodite-type phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: A lithium metal negative electrode having a protective layer with a thickness of 20 nm to 100 nm and a lithium metal battery including the same are provided. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. A silver or lithium nitride seed in the inorganic layer improves the wettability of molten lithium with a contact angle of 30 degrees or less. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the dendrite suppression of the lithium metal battery.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with a solid-state lithium battery using it. The precipitated beta-Li3PS4 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A solid-state lithium battery comprising the Li7P3S11 and LGPS material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 80:20, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. The precipitated Li7P3S11 phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The Li3PS4 and Li6PS5Cl composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The disclosure is applicable to beta-Li3PS4 and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 240 degrees C. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte with orthorhombic structure and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide solid electrolyte in which indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, InBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxidation stability limit is 4 V or more and the conductivity is 1.47 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved ionic conductivity and rate capability.

title: Method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Disclosed is a liquid-phase synthesis in which lithium sulfide and phosphorus pentasulfide react in a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran to give a sulfide solid electrolyte precursor. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The reaction at 65 degrees C to 100 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium hexafluorophosphate and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. The UV-crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The UV-crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength.

title: Multilayer solid electrolytic capacitor with improved heat resistance at 125 degrees C
abstract: A conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and a capacitor using the dispersion are provided. The dispersion of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) gives a uniform polymer layer and a high capacitance appearance rate for the 100 microfarad rating. The capacitor withstands 125 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) is doped with polystyrene sulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion. A solid electrolyte of poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The repair step reduces the leakage current and improves the reliability of the niobium capacitor. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the niobium anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage.

title: Slurry composition for a ceramic ion conductor layer using a nonpolar solvent and hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber
abstract: A slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer comprises ceramic ion conductor particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising xylene in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. An amorphous Li3PS4 glass with precipitated crystals is one example of a compatible conductor. The wet film is dried at 80 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 6 micrometers to 30 micrometers. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 15 micrometers and a conductivity of 2.5 mS/cm. In a solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sheet formability. A solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved sheet formability and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a mixed-halide ion-conductive solid of yttrium and hafnium that is stable against oxidation up to 4.2 V. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3InCl6. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 200 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. A battery using the halide in the positive electrode mixture shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Tin-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid tin binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. In an embodiment the ion-conductive solid layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 20 cm3/g or less. In an embodiment the material is beta-Li3PS4. A precursor of the Li3PS4 material obtained by ball milling of the starting materials is used. The Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. A crystallized Li2S-P2S5 glass containing a Li7P3S11 phase may be blended as a second conductor. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The soft-acid surface region improves the air stability and the moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride ceramic ion conductor with orthorhombic structure and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ceramic ion conductor in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. In the orthorhombic structure, yttrium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. Heat treatment at 200 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives an orthorhombic phase with a conductivity of 1.05 mS/cm or more. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A halogen-rich argyrodite-type with anion disorder is one option for the counterpart layer. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and styrene-butadiene rubber
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a solid electrolyte layer that has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The Li6PS5Cl and LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity.
