The binder content of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% gives a peel strength of 0.1 N/cm or more and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1500 mPa s to 6000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the layer shows improved ionic conductivity and a thin electrolyte layer.

title: Method of laminating an electrolyte layer and electrode layers for a solid-state cell
abstract: Disclosed is a method of manufacturing an electrode laminate by roll pressing at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C so that the electrode layers and the ion-conducting separator layer are bonded. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 100 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The current collector of stainless steel is used in a lithium battery with a 30 micrometer thick electrolyte sheet. The electrode laminate pressed at 100 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The lithium cobalt oxide electrode layer pressed at 25 degrees C keeps its contact during cycling. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 30 micrometers to 150 micrometers. The solid-state battery is restrained in a module at a stack pressure of 100 kPa.

title: Method for forming a solid electrolyte film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: A free-standing solid electrolyte sheet comprises solid electrolyte particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 50 micrometers after calendering. The LATP and Li7P3S11 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. Examples of the ion conductor include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7P3S11. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The powder is synthesized by a liquid-phase route in which the raw materials are dissolved in a solvent, precipitated, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The solvent-free sheet avoids the conductivity loss caused by polar solvents and improves the interfacial resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide solid electrolyte having a soft-acid surface region
abstract: Described is a moisture-resistant sulfide in which the soft acid silicon binds the sulfur and reduces reaction with water vapor. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The silicon substitution amount is 4 mol% to 16 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The low electronic conductivity of the Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A halide coating is compatible with the solid electrolyte because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. An H2S generation of 40 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 80% or more are obtained. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. The reaction at 10 degrees C to 45 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the sinterability. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved sinterability.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet ceramic ion conductor using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 10 mol%. The mixture for the ceramic ion conductor is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A hexachloride of yttrium or indium may serve as the catholyte. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3, LLZO, and LATP material. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. Examples of the ion conductor include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). The sintering aid lowers the sintering temperature by 100 degrees C or more while improving the ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide solid electrolyte whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO, LLZO, and Li2ZrO3 material. The disclosure is applicable to Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The oxidation potential is 5.2 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 5 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The surface region acts as an oxidation barrier and improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of the electrolyte layer.

title: Transition metal sulfide cathode material for a lithium ion battery and method of synthesizing the same
abstract: Provided is a core-shell cathode particle having a nickel sulfide core and a conductive carbon shell. The cathode with a loading of 5 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The initial capacity of 1000 mAh/g is retained with a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. The capacity retention after 500 cycles is 90% at 25 degrees C. The polar additive adsorbs polysulfides and improves the capacity retention to 90%. The carbon coating on the nickel sulfide composite has a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm and is formed by chemical vapor deposition of acetylene. The disclosure further provides a lithium battery in which the nickel sulfide cathode faces a lithium-containing negative electrode.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl propionate for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in ethyl propionate at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A solid-state battery comprising the Li6PS5Cl and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. Heat treatment at 500 degrees C after drying at 150 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The reaction is performed in a stirred reactor having a volume of 10 L or more, and the precipitate is washed with fresh solvent. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved moisture stability.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Hf(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The hafnium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 3 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved high-voltage stability and electrochemical window.

title: Wet coating method for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer on a release film and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a slurry for forming a ceramic ion conductor layer that has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s. The coating speed is 5 m/min and the layer dried at 60 degrees C to 100 degrees C has a thickness of 15 micrometers. The slurry has a solid content of 30 wt% to 50 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LiF and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The controlled viscosity gives a uniform thickness and improved ionic conductivity and dendrite suppression.

title: Stacked solid-state battery with bipolar current collectors and method of manufacturing the same
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 8 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar copper current collectors. The dry electrode process with styrene-butadiene rubber shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery. The primer layer on the copper foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The laminate is pressed by cold isostatic pressing at 100 MPa so that the interfaces between the layers are densified. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium iron phosphate and the battery is a lithium battery with 8 stacked cells. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 100 kPa through an elastic sheet. The all-solid-state battery is manufactured by stacking the layers and pressing them by cold isostatic pressing. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Sintering at 1150 degrees C with a lithium excess of 10 mol% gives a relative density of 95% and a conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm. A superionic argyrodite phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. After ball milling, the solid electrolyte precursor is pressed and sintered. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. Sintering is performed at 1150 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A lithium battery using the garnet sintered body as a separator shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and production method thereof
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 4.5 mS/cm. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The cubic argyrodite-type structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The powder is formed into a sheet by kneading with a fibrillated PTFE binder and roll-pressing without a solvent to a thickness of 30 micrometers to 80 micrometers. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane comprises a polyacrylonitrile matrix, lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide as the lithium salt, and tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether as a plasticizer. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 25 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. The polymer film serves as the solid electrolyte between the lithium metal and the positive electrode. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyacrylonitrile and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.5 mS/cm. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm are obtained.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNb(1-z)TazO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 80% or more and an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm is provided. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium niobium tantalum oxide (LiNb(1-z)TazO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The LiNbO3 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The reduction of the interfacial resistance is 50% or more, and the interfacial resistance after 50 cycles at 4.3 V is 30 ohm cm2 or less. A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. The material comprises lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. The high coverage of the coating results in improved cycle life at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Germanium-substituted phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid stable above 4.8 V and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a phosphate-based NASICON phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by germanium. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ion-conductive solid powder. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The oxidation potential is 4.8 V versus Li/Li+, the decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter, and the conductivity is 0.3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Suitable compositions include Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The LATP, Li2ZrO3, and LLTO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Amperometric carbon dioxide sensor using an oxide ion conducting ceramic and gas sensor system
abstract: This disclosure concerns a multilayer ceramic sensor element produced by co-firing green sheets of zirconia and alumina. The auxiliary electrode comprises lithium carbonate and is in contact with both the ceramic and the gas. The sensing electrode comprises lanthanum strontium manganite and a metal oxide and is printed on the ceramic and fired at 1000 degrees C. A solid electrolyte based sensor does not require a liquid electrolyte and operates at high temperature. The auxiliary electrode of lithium carbonate makes the sensor selective to carbon dioxide against interfering gases. The sensor is stable within 5% over 1000 hours at 300 degrees C. The multilayer structure with the gadolinium-doped ceria ceramic allows mass production by co-firing.

title: Lithium metal halide ceramic ion conductor represented by Li(3-z)In(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 for lithium battery
abstract: A rare earth metal halide ceramic ion conductor with cation disorder and a hexachloride framework is described. The median particle diameter D50 is 3 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, InCl3, and TiCl4 followed by heat treatment at 150 degrees C to 250 degrees C. In the trigonal structure, indium and titanium occupy octahedral sites of the close-packed chloride sublattice, and the cation disorder is 10% or more. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. The Li3InCl6, LiF, and Li3YCl6 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. In an embodiment the material is Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Method of manufacturing an electrode laminate for an all-solid-state battery by warm isostatic pressing
abstract: A stacked battery comprises 2 unit cells each having a positive electrode layer, a separator layer, and a negative electrode layer, the unit cells being stacked in series through bipolar nickel-plated copper current collectors. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 30 micrometers. The bipolar stacking of 2 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 25 degrees C after lamination. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium nickel cobalt manganese oxide and the battery is a lithium battery with 2 stacked cells. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The dry electrode process with polytetrafluoroethylene shortens the manufacturing time and avoids solvent recovery.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium yttrium chloride coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction and lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and nickel content of 75 mol% or more. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. The material comprises lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The air stability of the sulfide component is improved by oxygen substitution. An interlayer of a lithium-ion conductive polymer may be inserted to improve the contact at the interface. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate matrix. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 60 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The lithium salt is lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 100 micrometers. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The plasticizer succinonitrile enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 60 degrees C.

title: Iodine-substituted Li6PS5X solid electrolyte and lithium battery and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a Li6PS5X solid electrolyte in which part of the chlorine on the halogen site is replaced by iodine. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.4 to 1.8. The Li6PS5X crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The solid electrolyte is a lithium ion conducting material for a solid-state battery. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better ionic conductivity.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ion-conductive solid that does not require long mechanical milling. A solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A dry process in which the ion-conductive solid powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the solid-state battery. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state battery. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. The material comprises argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. A residual solvent content of 0.2 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Dry electrode manufacturing method using styrene-butadiene rubber and electrode produced thereby
abstract: A battery module with a restraining member that maintains a stack pressure of 500 kPa or more during cycling is described. The current collector is a copper foil of 10 micrometers to 20 micrometers thickness with a carbon primer layer. The electrode laminate pressed at 500 MPa and 25 degrees C has an interfacial resistance of 10 ohm cm2 or less. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The bipolar stacking of 16 cells raises the voltage of the battery without external wiring. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The edge of the 30 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. An all-solid-state battery comprising the laminate of 16 cells and a case is also provided.

title: Lithium niobium tantalum oxide-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a nickel-rich cathode material coated with lithium niobium tantalum oxide and to a method for producing the same. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium fluoride (LiF). The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The coated particles are heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the interfacial resistance and electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal halide solid electrolyte represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6 and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A halide solid electrolyte comprises a trigonal crystal phase of a lithium metal halide represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Ti(z)Cl6. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 350 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and Li3YCl6. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a trigonal phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid having argyrodite structure with controlled halogen occupancy and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a superionic sulfide of the argyrodite family in which halogen substitution exceeds the stoichiometric amount. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the solid-state lithium battery. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite phase is 0.075 or less. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 5.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by thermal evaporation and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LiF material. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 500 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.2% over 100 cycles. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The LiF layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the solid electrolyte at the negative electrode is suppressed and the dendrite suppression is improved.

title: Aluminum oxide deposited by atomic layer deposition protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The Al2O3 layer is amorphous and in direct contact with the metallic lithium, and the polymer layer faces the solid electrolyte. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the interfacial resistance. The protective layer thickness is 20 nm to 100 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.3% or more. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The suppression of filament penetration results in a longer cycle life and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobium tantalum oxide formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. The Li3InCl6 material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The coated particles are heat-treated at 300 degrees C to 400 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and production method thereof
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li3YCl6 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. In a solid-state lithium battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. The ion-conductive solid is preferably argyrodite Li6PS5Cl and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 75% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The sintering of a tantalum-doped garnet with a mother powder cover suppresses lithium volatilization. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment an interlayer comprising LiF and carbon is disposed on the surface facing the negative electrode. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the high-voltage stability is improved.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The oxide particles have a core of the titanium-free NASICON-type oxide phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Suitable compositions include Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.7 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5.2 V. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material comprises Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Battery module with a restraining member, an elastic sheet, and a cooling plate for 4 stacked cells
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 20 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by warm isostatic pressing and the release film is peeled. The lithium battery is operated at 80 degrees C under a stack pressure of 500 kPa. The primer layer on the stainless steel foil lowers the contact resistance and improves the rate capability. The edge of the 20 micrometer separator layer extends beyond the positive electrode layer by 0.5 mm to 2 mm to prevent contact with the negative electrode. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 20 micrometers. The positive electrode layer comprises lithium cobalt oxide, a conductive agent, and a binder, and has a thickness of 20 micrometers to 150 micrometers.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide solid electrolyte using ethyl propionate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide solid electrolyte powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The carbon content of the heat-treated powder is 0.3 wt% and the conductivity is 4.1 mS/cm. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, and beta-Li3PS4. After drying, the residual solvent content is 1 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in an all-solid-state battery. Because the raw materials react in the liquid phase, the method is scalable and gives a powder with improved sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte stable against oxidation above 4.8 V versus Li/Li+ comprises a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase in which part of the titanium is substituted by zirconium. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the LLTO and Li2ZrO3 material. An artificial interphase on the metallic lithium improves the wettability and suppresses filament growth. With zirconium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by zirconium in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Crystallized sulfide crystallized glass ion conductor containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase and method for producing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li7P3S11 material. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Halide ceramic ion conductor having a close-packed bromide sublattice and cation disorder
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Zr(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.2 to 0.45, and a method for producing the same are provided. The monoclinic phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The material is also used as a coating layer on core particles of a nickel-rich positive electrode active material, with a coverage of 85% or more and a thickness of 5 nm to 20 nm. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. In an all-solid-state lithium battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. After dehydration under vacuum at 300 degrees C, the water content is 0.5 wt% or less and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. The halide is useful as a catholyte and as a separator facing the positive electrode, with improved moisture stability and ionic conductivity.

title: Tantalum-doped garnet solid electrolyte sintered body with high relative density
abstract: A garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-v)La3Zr(2-v)Ta(v)O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The sintered body has a relative density of 96%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. The garnet grains are bonded through a thin lithium borate or lithium fluoride phase at the grain boundaries. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability.

title: Electrode for a solid-state battery with a aluminum current collector and a primer layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns a lamination method in which a transfer sheet of the 50 micrometer separator layer is pressed onto the electrode layer by uniaxial pressing and the release film is peeled. An insulating resin frame surrounds the electrode layers and is cured at 120 degrees C after lamination. The laminate of 16 cells forms a lithium battery whose negative electrode layer comprises silicon or lithium metal. The restraining member comprises end plates and bolts that apply a stack pressure of 500 kPa through an elastic sheet. The pressure jig keeps the stack pressure of 500 kPa uniform and improves the cycle life. The uniaxial pressing step at 500 MPa improves the contact between the layers and lowers the resistance of the cell. The separator layer transferred by pressing has a thickness variation of 5% or less at 50 micrometers.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ion-conductive solid having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and an oxygen-rich surface region is described. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 3.2 mS/cm. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. The LLZO material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 20 cm3/g. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The ion-conductive solid retains its conductivity after atmospheric exposure and shows improved sinterability and moisture stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with LiNbO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiNbO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide solid electrolyte. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a thio-LISICON phase
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 75:25 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. After heat treatment at 320 degrees C for 3 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 4 mS/cm. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. A layer cast from a heptane slurry and dried in an oven is one option for the separator layer. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. The glassy matrix absorbs volume change of the electrode and improves the ionic conductivity of the cell.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The disclosure is applicable to argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 1.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 5 mS/cm. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 80 degrees C to 160 degrees C under reduced pressure. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li6PS5Cl, LLZO, and Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide, and an initiator. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide salt gives a wide electrochemical window of 4.5 V in the polyacrylonitrile matrix. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The polymer electrolyte shows an ionic conductivity of 1.0 mS/cm at 60 degrees C and an electrochemical window of 4.5 V. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The polymer matrix is polyacrylonitrile and the ethylene oxide to lithium molar ratio is 12:1. The 20 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li7P3S11 crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 50%. The low electronic conductivity of the LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material makes it suitable for use in contact with a lithium metal anode. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 75:25, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The mixture for the solid electrolyte is subjected to ball milling in a planetary mill and then heat-treated. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The LGPS, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material is used in an all-solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li7P3S11 phase. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 2.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability and cycle life.

title: Dendrite-suppressing indium additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a method of operating a solid-state lithium cell under a stack pressure of 5 MPa to 20 MPa with an indium additive. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. Specific examples are Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The additive comprises indium in an amount of 0.8 wt% to 4 wt% and has an average particle size of 50 nm to 500 nm. The material comprises Li3YCl6 and beta-Li3PS4, and the electronic conductivity of the ceramic ion conductor layer is 1 x 10^-9 S/cm or less to prevent lithium deposition inside the layer. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. The plating overpotential is 30 mV or less and the Coulombic efficiency is 99% after 100 cycles. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor in which tin substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A solid-state battery comprising the LLZO and LLTO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Part of the titanium in the Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO phase is substituted by tin in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which raises the anodic stability. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 3 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 4.5 V. The widened electrochemical window improves the high-voltage stability and sinterability of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: Titanium-substituted lithium indium bromide ion-conductive solid with monoclinic structure for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a lithium indium bromide ion-conductive solid prepared by a water-mediated route and dehydrated under vacuum. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.1 to 0.35 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The ion-conductive solid is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF). A glass prepared by quenching and partially crystallized to a thio-LISICON phase can be used in the electrode mixture. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C for 2 hours to 12 hours gives a monoclinic phase with a conductivity of 0.56 mS/cm or more. The halide ion-conductive solid is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A solvent-free sheet formed by roll-pressing may be laminated onto the electrode. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 1.5 mol% to 6 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. The material conducts lithium ions and is used in a solid-state battery. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: A solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder from a suspension in an organic solvent is provided. The obtained powder is cast as a slurry in a nonpolar solvent with a rubber binder on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. Specific examples are Li7P3S11, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and beta-Li3PS4. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 1 mS/cm or more. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: GeS2-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A glassy sulfide ceramic ion conductor with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. The glass is heat-treated above its crystallization temperature so that a tetragonal or Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase precipitates uniformly. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 320 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 4 mS/cm. The LGPS, Li7P3S11, and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state lithium battery. The crystallized glass combines the deformability of a vitreous phase with the high conductivity of the crystal phase, improving the moisture stability.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with alumina nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: A single-ion conducting polymer electrolyte in which the anion is immobilized on the polymer backbone is provided. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained. The 30 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. The polymer solid electrolyte is used in an all-solid-state battery with a lithium metal negative electrode. A lithium secondary battery using the electrolyte shows a capacity retention of 85% after 200 cycles at 40 degrees C. alumina nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the germanium substitution and the surface region. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. In one embodiment the layer is produced by a dry process in which the mixture is rolled between heated rollers. In an embodiment the material is lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.5 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 5 V. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Argyrodite sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: This disclosure provides an argyrodite solid electrolyte whose anion sublattice is partially disordered by mixed chlorine-bromine substitution. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The bromine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the chlorine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). The argyrodite phase has a cubic lattice and a conductivity of 8.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C measured by AC impedance on a pressed pellet. The anion disorder lowers the activation barrier for lithium hopping and thereby improves the ionic conductivity.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide solid electrolyte with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and production method thereof
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for an all-solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x). In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li7P3S11 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved cycle life. The peak intensity ratio IA/IB of LiCl to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.08, and the room-temperature conductivity is 5.1 mS/cm. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite-type shows a higher conductivity and better cycle life.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3BO3 shell with high coverage and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium borate (Li3BO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. The ion-conductive component may be argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between ceramic ion conductor particles during pressing. Nickel accounts for 80 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 400 degrees C. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved cycle life.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 75:25 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. A halide coating is compatible with the ceramic ion conductor because both are stable against oxidation above 4 V. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). After heat treatment at 240 degrees C for 2 hours, the conductivity rises from 0.2 mS/cm for the glass to 1.8 mS/cm. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The layer may be a self-supporting film with a fibril network of polytetrafluoroethylene. A lithium secondary battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved electrochemical window and rate performance.

title: Li6PS5X sulfide ion-conductive solid with mixed chlorine-iodine substitution and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich Li6PS5X phosphosulfide having the composition Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)I(y) and to a lithium secondary battery comprising the same. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. When fired at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. The material comprises Li7P3S11 and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the Li6PS5X crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and iodine. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The material is useful as an ion-conductive solid layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and cycle life.

title: Aluminum-doped garnet ceramic ion conductor sintered body with high relative density and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A garnet-type oxide ceramic ion conductor comprises a sintered body of a cubic garnet phase represented by Li(7-3v)Al(v)La3Zr2O12 and Li2CO3 present at grain boundaries. Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A pellet of 500 micrometers thickness sintered at 1150 degrees C shows a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm and a relative density of 92%. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 2 micrometers to 15 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3YCl6 shell with high coverage
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. When combined with a halide coating on the cathode particles, the oxidative decomposition at high potential is further suppressed. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A coverage of 95% and a thickness of 5 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 60%. Dendrite growth is suppressed by an additive that promotes uniform deposition. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 95%. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The lithium yttrium chloride shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ion-conductive solid whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 92%. Dissolution of the raw materials in a nonaqueous solvent allows coating of the particles. The oxide particles have a core of the perovskite-type LLTO phase and a shell of 5 nm to 50 nm enriched in hafnium. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. A superionic Li6PS5X phosphosulfide may be mixed in as a second ion-conductive component. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The widened electrochemical window improves the grain boundary resistance of a high-voltage lithium battery.

title: lithium sulfide positive electrode material with a carbon coating and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Disclosed is a composite cathode in which lithium sulfide is confined in the pores of graphene to suppress the dissolution of polysulfides. The cathode with a loading of 3 mg/cm2 is combined with a lithium metal negative electrode and an ether-based electrolyte containing lithium nitrate. The confinement of lithium sulfide in the graphene suppresses the shuttle effect and improves the cycle life to 200 cycles. The composite shows a capacity of 1400 mAh/g at 0.2 C and a Coulombic efficiency of 98% or more. A solid-state lithium-sulfur battery comprising the cathode mixture, a sulfide solid electrolyte layer, and a lithium indium negative electrode is also provided. A lithium-sulfur pouch cell comprising the composite cathode and retaining 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles is also described. A separator coated with graphene traps the polysulfides on the cathode side. The carbon coating improves the electronic conductivity of the lithium sulfide cathode.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline ceramic ion conductor powder. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, YBr3, and TiBr4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. The disclosure further provides a solid-state lithium battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3InCl6, Li3YCl6, and LiF material. The water-mediated synthesis allows scalable production while retaining the ionic conductivity.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: A negative electrode structure for a battery comprising an ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium metal layer, an ion-conductive solid layer, and an additive comprising silver dispersed at the interface to form uniform nucleation sites. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li6PS5Cl material. The cell shows no short circuit for 500 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 5 MPa. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. A halide coating of Li3InCl6 or Li3YCl6 may be formed on the positive electrode active material to further lower the interfacial resistance. The suppression of void formation improves the interfacial resistance during fast charging.

title: Li2O-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: This disclosure concerns a Li2S-P2S5 glass of 70:30 composition that is converted by quenching and reheating into a crystallized conductor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. The oxidation stability against a high-voltage cathode is improved by an oxidation-resistant oxide component. The ion-conductive component may be Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A germanium-containing glass precursor gives a Li10GeP2S12-type crystal upon annealing at 260 degrees C. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor element with a polypyrrole layer and a carbon cathode layer
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of polypyrrole particles. The tantalum anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor. The capacitor has a capacitance of 470 microfarads, a rated voltage of 10 V, and an equivalent series resistance of 10 milliohms at 100 kHz. The capacitor rated at 10 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. A solid electrolyte of polypyrrole replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor. The polypyrrole is doped with p-toluenesulfonate and has a particle size of 20 nm to 100 nm in the dispersion.

title: Solid oxide electrolysis cell and reversible fuel cell having a thin dense electrolyte
abstract: A method for manufacturing a solid oxide fuel cell by tape casting a yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte green sheet and laminating it on an anode support green body is provided. A diffusion barrier layer of gadolinium-doped ceria is disposed between the yttria-stabilized zirconia electrolyte and the lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite cathode to prevent the formation of strontium zirconate. The stack shows stable operation over 100 thermal cycles without gas leakage at 650 to 800 degrees C. The interconnect is a ferritic stainless steel plate coated with a manganese cobalt spinel to suppress chromium evaporation at 650 to 800 degrees C. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C. The cell can be operated at 650 to 800 degrees C, which allows the use of metal interconnects.

title: Ceramic ion conductor sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ceramic ion conductor sheet comprises ceramic ion conductor particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. With a binder content of 1 wt% and a roll temperature of 60 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less.
