A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ceramic ion conductor can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. No solvent is used in the process, so the ceramic ion conductor does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. The sheet can be laminated onto an electrode without a drying step and improves the interfacial resistance of the cell.

title: Lithium zirconate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide ceramic ion conductor includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 80% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 85%. A sulfide synthesized by the liquid-phase method is one example of a compatible conductor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li2ZrO3 material. Suitable compositions include lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). A coverage of 85% and a thickness of 15 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 40%. The lithium zirconate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and method for preparing the same
abstract: Provided is a phosphate-based NASICON ion-conductive solid in which germanium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. With germanium substitution of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, the oxidation potential rises by 0.4 V or more compared with the unsubstituted oxide. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ion-conductive solid. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. Because oxidative decomposition is suppressed, the interfacial resistance growth is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Protective layer suppressing lithium filament penetration and method for forming the same
abstract: Disclosed is a bilayer protective layer that suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments into an ion-conductive solid layer and stabilizes the interface with metallic lithium. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry may contain a dispersant and have a solid content of about 60 wt%. The inorganic layer has a thickness of 200 nm and the polymer layer has a thickness of 0.5 micrometers, giving an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.5% over 100 cycles. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. Because the inorganic layer blocks electron leakage, the decomposition of the ion-conductive solid at the negative electrode is suppressed and the cycle life is improved.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor with low residual solvent for lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. After drying, the residual solvent content is 0.2 wt% or less and the carbon content is 0.5 wt% or less. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm or more. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The Li7P3S11, Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a lithium secondary battery. The material comprises Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. A glass ceramic containing a crystalline phase in a glass matrix is preferred because of its deformability. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the grain boundary resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant gallium stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. Sintering at 1250 degrees C with a lithium excess of 15 mol% gives a relative density of 94% and a conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and grain boundary resistance.

title: Slurry composition for a solid electrolyte layer using a nonpolar solvent and polyisobutylene
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The solvent has a donor number of 10 or less so that the solid electrolyte does not react with the solvent during slurry processing. Atmospheric exposure at a dew point of -30 degrees C does not reduce the conductivity by more than 20%. Densification of the garnet by hot pressing improves the contact with the material. A lithium secondary battery comprising the LATP, Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), beta-Li3PS4, and Li7P3S11. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the solid electrolyte in the lithium secondary battery. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 50 micrometers. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability and ionic conductivity.

title: Solid electrolytic capacitor having a porous tantalum anode body and a hybrid electrolyte
abstract: A solid electrolytic capacitor includes a porous tantalum anode body, a dielectric oxide film formed on the anode body, a conductive polymer layer comprising polypyrrole doped with naphthalenesulfonate, a carbon layer, and a silver layer. The capacitor withstands 150 degrees C for 1000 hours with a capacitance change of 10% or less. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 150 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. The dielectric oxide film is formed by anodizing the tantalum anode body in a phosphoric acid solution at a formation voltage of 2 to 4 times the rated voltage. The naphthalenesulfonate doped polymer keeps its conductivity after 150 degrees C storage. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. A solid electrolyte of polypyrrole replaces the liquid electrolyte of a conventional electrolytic capacitor.

title: Additive combination for a non-aqueous electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a non-aqueous electrolyte for a lithium ion battery with improved storage characteristics at 60 degrees C. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. The combination of tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. A second additive selected from 1,3-propane sultone and succinonitrile is added in an amount of 1 wt% to suppress the dissolution of transition metals from the positive electrode. A lithium secondary battery comprising the electrolyte and a silicon-containing negative electrode is also described. The 1.2 M electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a viscosity of 4 cP or less. The stable passivation film formed by tris(trimethylsilyl) phosphite suppresses the consumption of the electrolyte and improves the cycle life to 300 cycles.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. A core-shell cathode particle with a nanometer-thick LiNbO3 coating of high coverage is used on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The ion-conductive component may be Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). With a binder content of 3 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 20% or less. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ion-conductive solid. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved high-voltage stability and grain boundary resistance.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 20:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 20 micrometers. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The membrane has a tensile strength of 2 MPa or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm at 40 degrees C. The anion is covalently bonded to the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide solid electrolyte and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide solid electrolyte that remains stable up to 5.2 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The argyrodite-type phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. In a solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. Reduction of titanium at 1.5 V versus Li/Li+ is suppressed by the hafnium substitution and the surface region. The oxide solid electrolyte enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide ion-conductive solid with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from acetonitrile, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 140 degrees C to 220 degrees C under reduced pressure. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The low residual solvent suppresses the decrease in conductivity caused by carbon-containing impurities and improves the moisture stability.

title: Method for suppressing lithium filament growth using a zinc-containing additive layer
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the solid electrolyte. A Coulombic efficiency of 99% or more and a critical current density of 1 mA/cm2 are obtained at 25 degrees C. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising the LLZO, Li3YCl6, and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state lithium battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The anodic decomposition at high voltage is suppressed when an oxidation-resistant oxide is used. A stack pressure of 1 MPa to 4 MPa is applied so that void formation at the interface during stripping is suppressed. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. An all-solid-state lithium battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The suppression of void formation improves the ionic conductivity and interfacial resistance during fast charging.

title: Liquid-phase synthesis of a sulfide ceramic ion conductor using ethyl acetate for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a liquid-phase route to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor that does not require long mechanical milling. Specific examples are argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li7P3S11, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C after drying at 200 degrees C gives a conductivity of 2.9 mS/cm or more. The powder may be formed into a free-standing sheet using a fibrillated PTFE binder without a solvent. The suspension has a solid concentration of 4 wt% to 16 wt% and is reacted at 25 degrees C to 60 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved sinterability. The solvent is ethyl acetate, and LiCl or LiBr dissolved in the solvent is incorporated into the precipitate. A lithium secondary battery using the ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method shows improved sinterability.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a densified garnet-type oxide solid electrolyte and to a lithium battery including the same. Mechanical mixing by ball milling under an inert atmosphere is applied to the raw material mixture. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The amount of the sintering aid is 2 wt%, the sintering temperature is 1250 degrees C, and the resulting density is 96%. Sintering is performed at 1250 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A sintering aid comprising LiF is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Suitable compositions include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the ionic conductivity. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the ionic conductivity of the garnet layer.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Provided is a sulfide ion-conductive solid that retains 75% or more of its conductivity after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C for 6 hours. The positive electrode active material is preferably provided with a halide coating having a thickness of 5 nm to 30 nm. The substitution amount is 2 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm or more. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. The arsenic-free antimony substitution amount is 1 mol% to 4 mol%, and the substituting element is concentrated in a surface region of 2 nm to 30 nm. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. The suppressed H2S generation results in improved sinterability and grain boundary resistance and simpler handling.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a coated positive electrode active material whose LiTaO3 shell suppresses the interfacial reaction with a sulfide solid electrolyte. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The LiNbO3, Li2ZrO3, Li6PS5Cl, and LiF material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. A halide conductor of the hexachloride type with cation disorder forms part of the composition, so that the material is both a coating and a halide conductor. A coverage of 90% and a thickness of 3 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 50%. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. The high coverage of the coating results in improved high-voltage stability at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The coating layer further contains boron in an amount of 0.01 wt% to 0.5 wt% relative to the core particles. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The coated particles have a specific surface area of 0.3 m2/g to 1.5 m2/g and the shell thickness is 5 nm. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). A lithium secondary battery using the coated active material shows improved high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Method for forming a conductive polymer layer on a dielectric oxide of a solid electrolytic capacitor
abstract: Disclosed is a method for forming a conductive polymer layer by impregnating a dielectric-coated anode body with a dispersion of polyaniline particles. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polyaniline layer to serve as the cathode lead-out. The capacitor shows improved heat resistance at 105 degrees C and can be mounted by reflow soldering. A capacitance of 100 microfarads is obtained in a case size of 7.3 mm by 4.3 mm. The conductive polymer layer contains a polyhydric alcohol as an additive that improves the coverage on the dielectric. The niobium anode body with the polymer cathode gives a volumetric efficiency higher than a liquid electrolyte capacitor.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide solid electrolyte and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte in which a thio-LISICON type crystal is embedded in a glass is described, together with an all-solid-state battery using it. Ball milling of the raw materials for the Li3PS4 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 280 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 2.5 mS/cm. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Crystallization is performed at 240 degrees C to 320 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 4 hours, which precipitates a Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The solid electrolyte shows improved electrochemical window and moisture stability compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Polymer electrolyte membrane with titania nanoparticles and battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The disclosure further provides a lithium ion battery whose separator is replaced by the polymer electrolyte membrane. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer. The plasticizer tetraethylene glycol dimethyl ether enables operation of the polymer electrolyte cell at 25 degrees C. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided. The membrane of 100 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.2 mS/cm are obtained.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: A polymer electrolyte membrane containing silica nanoparticles that disrupt the crystallinity of the polymer is described. A pouch type lithium battery comprising the semi-interpenetrating polymer electrolyte and a graphite negative electrode is also described. The 50 micrometer membrane is flexible and suitable for a pouch cell. silica nanoparticles with a diameter of 10 nm to 50 nm are dispersed in the polymer in an amount of 5 wt% to 15 wt%. The lithium salt is lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide and the membrane has a thickness of 50 micrometers. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 12:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained.

title: Dendrite-suppressing lithium fluoride additive at the lithium metal interface of a solid-state cell and production method thereof
abstract: A lithium metal interface with uniform nucleation and suppressed dendrite penetration along grain boundaries is described. The wet film is peeled from the support film after drying. The suspension route avoids long milling and gives a homogeneous powder. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. With the additive in an amount of 0.5 wt% and a stack pressure of 2 MPa, the Coulombic efficiency is 99%. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the dendrite suppression.

title: Conductive polymer dispersion for a solid electrolytic capacitor and capacitor using the same
abstract: A hybrid capacitor combining a conductive polymer layer and an electrolytic solution is described. The equivalent series resistance is 20 milliohms or less and the leakage current is 0.01 CV or less. The polyaniline layer lowers the equivalent series resistance to 20 milliohms compared with manganese dioxide. The capacitor rated at 25 V can be used in a power supply circuit of an electronic device with a low ripple voltage. The solid electrolyte is the conductive polymer layer that serves as the true cathode of the capacitor. The conductive polymer layer is formed by chemical polymerization of the monomer in the presence of an oxidant followed by impregnation with a polymer dispersion. A carbon layer and a silver paste layer are formed on the polyaniline layer to serve as the cathode lead-out.

title: Oxide solid electrolyte having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a perovskite-type LLTO solid electrolyte in which zirconium substitution raises the oxidation potential and suppresses titanium reduction. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 88%. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved sinterability.

title: Negative electrode structure with uniform lithium nucleation and high critical current density
abstract: Disclosed is a dendrite-suppressing structure in which a magnesium-containing additive at the lithium interface raises the critical current density. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3YCl6 material. The Li3YCl6 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. The additive forms an alloy with lithium during plating, which provides uniform nucleation sites and suppresses filament formation. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. The critical current density at 25 degrees C is 2 mA/cm2 and the cell survives 1000 cycles of plating and stripping without short circuit. The resulting Li3YCl6 material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. Because nucleation is uniform, the local current density is reduced and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ion-conductive solid obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-LiI glass. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The ion-conductive component may be Li3InCl6, lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Uniform nucleation of lithium during plating raises the critical current density of the cell. A lithium secondary battery comprising the Li3InCl6, Li2ZrO3, and Li6PS5Cl material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The precipitated thio-LISICON phase has an average crystallite size of 50 nm, and the material shows a conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm. Crystallization is performed at 260 degrees C to 340 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 12 hours, which precipitates a thio-LISICON phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the cycle life is retained.

title: Lithium secondary battery with reduced gas generation during high temperature storage
abstract: Described is a combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive for a non-aqueous electrolyte. A lithium ion battery containing the electrolyte with 3 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate is also described. The combination of fluoroethylene carbonate and a sulfur-containing additive improves both the cycle life and the low temperature performance. The negative electrode comprises graphite and silicon oxide, and the positive electrode comprises a nickel-rich layered oxide charged to 4.3 V. The electrolyte containing lithium hexafluorophosphate is injected into a pouch cell and the cell is formed at 0.1 C for the first cycle. With 3 wt% of fluoroethylene carbonate, the capacity retention after 500 cycles is 92% and the gas generation is reduced by 40%. The fluorinated solvent improves the oxidation stability of the electrolyte at 4.3 V.

title: Wet coating method for forming an ion-conductive solid layer on a release film
abstract: Described is a slurry composition using a nonpolar solvent that does not react with the sulfide and a binder soluble in the solvent. The disclosure further provides a lithium secondary battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4, Li6PS5Cl, and LLZO material. A Li6PS5X sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The slurry has a solid content of 60 wt% and a viscosity of 3000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm. The ion-conductive component may be beta-Li3PS4, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The binder is polyisobutylene in an amount of 0.4 wt% to 2 wt% and is dissolved in the nonpolar solvent xylene. The dispersant prevents agglomeration and improves the cycle life and ionic conductivity of the layer.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and production method thereof
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide ceramic ion conductor whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 40 cm3/g or less. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -40 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C, and the conductivity is 1.6 mS/cm or more. The Li6PS5Cl material is used in a lithium secondary battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 40 cm3/g or less. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A lithium secondary battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved moisture stability.

title: Arsenic-free antimony-substituted sulfide ion-conductive solid with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and method for producing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The substitution amount is 8 mol%, the heat treatment temperature is 500 degrees C, and the conductivity is 2.2 mS/cm or more. Oxygen substitution of part of the sulfur forms P-O bonds that are stable against hydrolysis. The method further comprises forming a free-standing sheet from the powder by calendering with a fibril binder network. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. A solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), Li7P3S11, argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl, and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), and the H2S generation measured in a 1 L sealed chamber at 25 degrees C is 10 cm3/g or less. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A solid-state battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Positive electrode active material with lithium niobium tantalum oxide coating layer suppressing interfacial reaction
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous LiNb(1-z)TazO3 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. A powder-to-film process with heated rollers is one option for forming the layer. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor. Because the shell is amorphous and continuous, the growth of interfacial resistance is reduced and the interfacial resistance is improved.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by oxygen and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11, Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS), and beta-Li3PS4. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 0.5 micrometers and a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state lithium battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. A solid-state lithium battery using the moisture-stable sulfide shows improved ionic conductivity.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 10 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 90%. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. A stack pressure of a few MPa suppresses void formation during stripping. A solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The hafnium substitution suppresses titanium reduction and improves the grain boundary resistance in contact with lithium.

title: Method for forming an ion-conductive solid film by powder-to-film rolling without solvent
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a self-supporting ion-conductive solid film produced by powder-to-film rolling and calendering. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. An argyrodite-type phase with partial bromine substitution on the halogen site may be added as a conductive additive. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The kneading is performed at a shear rate of 100 s^-1 to 1000 s^-1 so that the PTFE is fibrillized into a network. With a binder content of 2 wt% and a roll temperature of 80 degrees C, the sheet has a porosity of 16% or less. No solvent is used in the process, so the ion-conductive solid does not react with a polar solvent and retains its conductivity. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The low porosity results in a low areal resistance and improved sheet formability.

title: Silver-carbon composite protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to an artificial interphase formed on a lithium metal negative electrode by solution casting. The disclosure is applicable to Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The protective layer thickness is 120 nm to 600 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 98.5% or more. The material comprises Li3YCl6, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The protective layer is deposited on a lithium foil of 20 micrometers thickness under an argon atmosphere. The cubic argyrodite structure tolerates chlorine and bromine on the 4a and 4d sites. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. A dry process is preferred for forming the ceramic ion conductor sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An all-solid-state battery comprising the Li3YCl6, Li3PS4, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The lithiophilic interphase gives uniform lithium deposition and improved cycle life.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. The ceramic ion conductor obtained by the method has an ionic conductivity of 4.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a residual solvent content of 0.3 wt%. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li7P3S11. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The suspension has a solid concentration of 2.5 wt% to 10 wt% and is reacted at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C with stirring for 6 hours to 72 hours. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of a Li6PS5X component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The wet-chemical process is suitable for coating an active material and improves the grain boundary resistance and moisture stability.

title: Composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer and a lithium salt
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a gel polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide for a lithium secondary battery and to a method of forming it in situ inside the cell. The anion is covalently bonded to the polycarbonate chain, which gives a lithium transference number of 0.8 or more. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polycarbonate. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1 balances conductivity and mechanical strength. The membrane of 30 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polycarbonate and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of a Li2S-P2S5 glass and lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sulfide ceramic ion conductor obtained by controlled crystallization of an amorphous Li2S-P2S5-Li2O glass. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. The disclosure further provides a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. The heat treatment time is 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which gives a crystallinity of 40% to 75% by X-ray diffraction. A perovskite-type LLTO or a phosphate-based oxide may be added as a catholyte stable above 4.5 V. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Air-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid having a soft-acid surface region and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. Heat treatment at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The surface region is enriched in a soft-acid element so that the hydrolysis of the sulfide by water vapor is suppressed. The LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The LLZO composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. A zirconium-substituted Li2ZrCl6-type halide is one option for the counterpart layer. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLZO material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Because H2S generation is reduced, the safety of the manufacturing process and the grain boundary resistance are improved.

title: Bilayer protection of metallic lithium with an inorganic LiF layer and a fluorinated polymer
abstract: Described is an inorganic-polymer bilayer that protects the lithium metal negative electrode against the ceramic ion conductor. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The LiF and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state battery. The ceramic ion conductor is preferably lithium fluoride (LiF) and beta-Li3PS4. H2S generation upon exposure to humid air is reduced when a soft-acid element is present at the surface. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. A solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ceramic ion conductor shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 100 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.5 micrometers to 3 micrometers. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. The protective layer is useful for an anode-free cell, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sintering method for a garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder cover and a lithium excess of 5 mol%. Sintering is performed at 1100 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. A halide with a close-packed chloride sublattice and octahedral yttrium is one example of an oxidation-stable conductor. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The sintered body has a relative density of 97%, an average grain size of 2 micrometers, and a total conductivity of 0.4 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. The cell may employ a lithium metal anode, a lithium alloy anode, or a silicon-containing anode. The sintered body consists of garnet grains having an average grain size of 0.8 micrometers to 6 micrometers and a tetragonal garnet phase of 3% or less. The low grain boundary resistance results in improved high-voltage stability and sinterability compared with a garnet sintered without the aid.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: An oxide ion-conductive solid that remains stable up to 4.8 V and a lithium battery with a high-voltage cathode are provided. The oxide has an ionic conductivity of 0.3 mS/cm and an electrochemical window of 1.8 V to 4.8 V. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of a lithium secondary battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. Slurry casting with a controlled solid content forms the layer on a release film. The lithium secondary battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Method for producing an ion-conductive solid sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: A slurry for forming an ion-conductive solid layer comprises ion-conductive solid particles, a hydrogenated nitrile butadiene rubber binder, a nonpolar solvent comprising a mixed solvent of toluene and heptane in which the binder is dissolved, and a dispersant. The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The slurry has a solid content of 40 wt% to 60 wt% and a viscosity of 500 mPa s to 2000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. The slurry is applied onto a release film at a coating speed of 1 m/min to 10 m/min and dried at 40 degrees C to 80 degrees C in an oven. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, and the dried layer has a thickness of 30 micrometers and a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the all-solid-state battery. The slurry allows roll-to-roll production of the layer and improves the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window of the cell.

title: Zirconium-substituted lithium indium bromide solid electrolyte with monoclinic structure and method for preparing the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed bromide anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The material comprises lithium fluoride (LiF) and Li3InCl6, and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 3 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.5 V versus Li/Li+. An argyrodite-type sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the electrochemical window.

title: Garnet-type Li7La3Zr2O12 ceramic ion conductor with reduced grain boundary resistance and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: A sintered garnet pellet with a relative density of 92% and a method of hot pressing the same are described. A crystallized glass with a tetragonal phase may be added to improve the conductivity of the mixture. An all-solid-state lithium battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The coating layer on the cathode particle suppresses the interfacial reaction with the sulfide. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). A sintering aid comprising Li2CO3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. When v is 0.3, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.6 mS/cm. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the sinterability and ionic conductivity.

title: Polymer electrolyte with a plasticizer for room temperature operation of a lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a composition for a polymer electrolyte comprising a crosslinkable monomer, lithium perchlorate, and an initiator. The silica nanoparticles improve the conductivity by disrupting the crystallinity of polyethylene oxide. The cell with the polymer electrolyte retains 85% of its capacity after 200 cycles at 25 degrees C. The polymer electrolyte is laminated with a thin ceramic ion conductor layer to block dendrites. The polyethylene oxide electrolyte suppresses leakage and improves the safety of the lithium battery. The membrane of 20 micrometers is formed by casting a solution of polyethylene oxide and the salt in acetonitrile and drying under vacuum. The polymer electrolyte containing lithium perchlorate is used in a lithium secondary battery operated at 25 degrees C. The plasticizer succinonitrile is added in an amount of 10 wt% to 40 wt% to lower the glass transition temperature of the polymer.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of indium and hafnium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is a monoclinic halide solid electrolyte in which indium and hafnium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.1 to 0.35. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The halide is applied to the positive electrode active material by a wet coating with an alkoxide-free solution, giving a coated cathode. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The ion-conductive component may be Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Also described is a solid-state lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The material comprises Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the hexachloride framework tolerates partial substitution by scandium or a rare earth element. Because the chloride framework is oxidation-resistant, the moisture stability at 4.3 V is improved.

title: Halogen-rich argyrodite-type ceramic ion conductor having anion disorder
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). The ceramic ion conductor is preferably Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The electrode mixture of the solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The argyrodite-type crystal phase accounts for 90% or more of the crystalline phases, the balance being a trace of LiCl and Li3PS4. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4, wherein the argyrodite-type crystal phase is superionic and the anion sublattice contains sulfur, chlorine, and bromine. A solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. When fired at 470 degrees C to 570 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 8.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. The material is useful as a ceramic ion conductor layer or as an ion conductor in an electrode mixture, with improved electrochemical window and ionic conductivity.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of scandium and zirconium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: Provided is an orthorhombic halide ceramic ion conductor in which scandium and zirconium occupy octahedral sites of a close-packed chloride lattice. A coated NCM cathode with a shell of 5 nm to 10 nm is one example of a compatible positive electrode. A coating layer of the halide on the active material lowers the interfacial resistance with the sulfide, and the coverage is determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Specific examples are lithium fluoride (LiF), Li3YCl6, and lithium niobate (LiNbO3). The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiCl, ScCl3, and ZrCl4 followed by heat treatment at 250 degrees C to 350 degrees C. The zirconium substitution in an amount z of 0.2 to 0.45 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. The Li6PS5X phase may be combined with a halogen-rich sulfide to raise the superionic conductivity. A cation disorder of 15% and a conductivity of 3 mS/cm are obtained at z of 0.2 to 0.45. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiF, Li3YCl6, and LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The close-packed anion sublattice gives a low activation energy and improved electrochemical window.

title: Mixed-halide solid electrolyte of yttrium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: A halide ion conductor having the composition Li(3-z)Y(1-z)Ti(z)Br6, wherein z is 0.3 to 0.55, and a method for producing the same are provided. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A metastable crystal phase precipitated in a glass gives a conductivity above that of the glass itself. The median particle diameter D50 is 2 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. The halide phase is free of a LiBr secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The titanium substitution in an amount z of 0.3 to 0.55 introduces lithium vacancies that raise the ionic conductivity of the metal halide. Compared with Li3YCl6, the substituted halide shows higher conductivity and better moisture stability.

title: Solid-state lithium cell with improved plating and stripping stability under stack pressure
abstract: This disclosure concerns an additive that alloys with lithium during plating and prevents short circuit through the ion-conductive solid. A gallium-doped garnet sintered body is one option for the oxide component. The electrode mixture of the lithium secondary battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The Li3YCl6, LiF, and Li3PS4 material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Suitable compositions include Li3YCl6, lithium fluoride (LiF), and beta-Li3PS4. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. During stripping, the alloy phase of the additive keeps the contact and suppresses void growth. Lithium penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed because the nucleation is uniform and the current density is below the critical value. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the ion-conductive solid in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The cell shows no short circuit for 200 cycles at 1 mA/cm2 and 1 mAh/cm2 under a stack pressure of 10 MPa. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. The alloy formation lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the ionic conductivity.

title: LiI-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: An amorphous sulfide containing germanium or silicon sulfide is crystallized to form a ceramic ion conductor of high conductivity. An activation energy of 0.25 eV or less and a conductivity of 3.8 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C are obtained. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. The vitreous precursor is obtained by melt quenching or mechanical amorphization and has a glass transition temperature of 180 degrees C to 230 degrees C. The crystal phase precipitated in the glass is thio-LISICON, and a Li4P2S6 phase formed by devitrification is 5% or less. An all-solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved electrochemical window. In an embodiment the material is argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The halogen occupancy and anion disorder of an argyrodite-type component can be adjusted to tune the conductivity. The ceramic ion conductor shows improved electrochemical window and cycle life compared with a fully crystalline powder of the same composition.

title: Solution-based process for preparing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor powder for lithium battery
abstract: A method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor by stirring the raw materials in 1,2-dimethoxyethane at 25 degrees C and filtering the precipitate is described. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The dried precursor is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C for 1 hour to 6 hours and shows a conductivity of 3.5 mS/cm or more. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The rare earth halide component is stable against oxidation and tolerates cation disorder. The dried precipitate is heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an argon atmosphere to convert the complex into the crystalline sulfide. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. The liquid-phase route yields fine particles with a narrow size distribution and improved grain boundary resistance and ionic conductivity.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li2WO4 shell with high coverage for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium tungstate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 90%. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a solid electrolyte layer disposed therebetween is also provided. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. The material comprises Li3InCl6, and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. Nickel accounts for 85 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 300 degrees C. The solid electrolyte is preferably Li3InCl6. The coating layer suppresses interfacial reactions between the high-nickel active material and the sulfide, improving the high-voltage stability.

title: Gel polymer electrolyte comprising poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate and lithium bis(fluorosulfonyl)imide and lithium secondary battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a solid polymer electrolyte film with an ethylene oxide to lithium ratio of 8:1. The thermally crosslinked network improves the mechanical strength while keeping the conductivity at 0.1 mS/cm. The electrolyte is polymerized in situ at 40 degrees C after the cell is assembled, so that the contact with the electrodes is intimate. Also provided is a lithium battery in which the poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate based electrolyte of 100 micrometers is sandwiched between a positive electrode and a lithium metal negative electrode. The in situ polymerization gives low interfacial resistance with the electrodes and a thickness of 100 micrometers. A lithium transference number of 0.5 or more and a conductivity of 0.1 mS/cm are obtained. The thermally crosslinked network is formed by irradiating the composition with ultraviolet light for 1 minute to 10 minutes. A composite electrolyte in which an inorganic ion conductor such as LLZO or LATP is dispersed in the polymer is also provided.

title: Halogen-rich Li6PS5X solid electrolyte having anion disorder and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A Li6PS5X solid electrolyte represented by Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Cl(1+x) and a method for producing the same are described. A pellet pressed from the powder has a density of 1.85 g/cm3 or more and shows a conductivity of 9.6 mS/cm. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the solid electrolyte shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. The solid electrolyte is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and Li7P3S11. Because the lithium halide impurity is suppressed, the moisture stability of the material is retained after storage.

title: P2O5-containing vitreous sulfide ceramic ion conductor and heat treatment method
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor comprises a glass phase of Li2S and P2S5 in a molar ratio of 70:30 and a beta-Li3PS4 crystal phase precipitated therein. The LGPS material is used in a solid-state lithium battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. The content of P2O5 is 8 mol%, the crystallization temperature is 240 degrees C, and the conductivity is 3.8 mS/cm or more. The fibrillization of the binder under shear gives a free-standing film. Crystallization is performed at 200 degrees C to 280 degrees C for 0.5 hours to 20 hours, which precipitates a beta-Li3PS4 phase with a crystallite size of 20 nm to 200 nm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ceramic ion conductor layer of the solid-state lithium battery. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. An interlayer formed by sputtering is used to suppress the side reaction at the interface. The disclosure is applicable to Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). Because the crystal phase is precipitated inside the glass, the grain boundary resistance is small and the ionic conductivity is improved.

title: Silicon-substituted sulfide solid electrolyte with suppressed hydrogen sulfide generation and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a sulfide solid electrolyte whose hydrogen sulfide generation upon exposure to humid air is 20 cm3/g or less. Heat treatment at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C gives a conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm and a retention of 85% after humid exposure. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 350 degrees C to 450 degrees C. The ion-conductive component may be Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3). Ball milling with zirconia balls at 300 rpm to 600 rpm is used to obtain an amorphous precursor. An amorphous zirconate or tantalate shell on the nickel-rich active material suppresses the space-charge layer. The lanthanum zirconium garnet may be sintered at 1150 degrees C using a sintering aid. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The powder is hygroscopic to an extent of 1 wt% or less of water uptake at 10% relative humidity. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the high-voltage stability.

title: Hafnium-substituted lithium yttrium chloride solid electrolyte with trigonal structure and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Disclosed is a halide solid electrolyte in which hafnium is substituted for part of the yttrium in a lithium yttrium chloride framework. The metal halide particles have a median diameter D50 of 0.15 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers and are mixed with the positive electrode active material without a coating. The halide solid electrolyte has an ionic conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.3 V versus Li/Li+. Cyclic voltammetry confirms that the oxide component is stable up to 5 V. The negative electrode may be metallic lithium with a fluorinated protective layer. The disclosure is applicable to Li3InCl6. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. The halide phase is free of a LiCl secondary phase and has a crystallite size of 30 nm to 300 nm. The halide solid electrolyte is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the moisture stability and high-voltage stability.

title: Method for producing a ceramic ion conductor sheet by slurry casting and peeling
abstract: Disclosed is a wet coating method in which a slurry of a ceramic ion conductor is cast on a release film by a doctor blade and dried to form a layer. The dried layer shows an ionic conductivity of 0.6 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C and a thickness of 15 micrometers. The LLZO and Li6PS5Cl material is also useful as a protective layer between a lithium metal anode and a sulfide layer. Also described is an all-solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The release film is a PET film having a silicone release layer, and the dried layer is peeled from the release film and pressed onto an electrode. A sputtered inorganic protective layer of 100 nm may be used between the lithium and the material. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted argyrodite having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. The peeling from the release film gives a transferable sheet and improved cycle life.

title: Ion-conductive solid sheet formed by kneading and roll-pressing and solid-state battery
abstract: Provided is a sheet in which ion-conductive solid particles are held by PTFE fibrils formed by fibrillization during kneading. A dew point controlled atmosphere is used during processing to avoid hydrolysis. The roll temperature is 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C and the sheet has a thickness of 80 micrometers after calendering. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. Specific examples are Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The ion-conductive solid is applied as the electrolyte of an all-solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. The kneaded mixture is rolled between rollers at 70 degrees C to 130 degrees C, and the roller gap is reduced stepwise in at least three passes. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The fibrillated binder gives a flexible sheet and improved interfacial resistance.

title: Method for sintering a cubic garnet solid electrolyte using a mother powder
abstract: Disclosed is a method for sintering a gallium-doped Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet to a relative density of 91% or more while suppressing lithium volatilization. Sintering is performed at 1230 degrees C for 4 hours to 12 hours in an alumina crucible under a bed of the mother powder. The resulting LATP and LLTO material is compatible with a dry process for electrode and separator layer fabrication. In an embodiment the material is Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). The mother powder has a median particle diameter D50 of 3 micrometers, and the sintered body has a conductivity of 0.8 mS/cm. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The raw materials of the solid electrolyte are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. Also described is a lithium secondary battery comprising the solid electrolyte in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. A wet slurry process with a doctor blade on a release film may be used to form the layer. The dense garnet body suppresses lithium penetration along grain boundaries and improves the grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor resistant to hydrolysis under humid air and method for preparing the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a sulfide ion conductor with suppressed H2S generation and a method for producing the same. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ceramic ion conductor layer onto an electrode of the solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The water uptake at 10% relative humidity is 0.5 wt% and the conductivity is 1 mS/cm. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the ceramic ion conductor is improved. An argyrodite sulfide of the Li5.5PS4.5Cl1.5 type is one example of a compatible ion conductor. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -40 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. After ball milling, the ceramic ion conductor precursor is pressed and sintered. The suppressed hydrolysis allows the sulfide to be handled in a dry room instead of a glove box, improving the ionic conductivity and moisture stability.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite-type solid electrolyte and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a halogen-rich argyrodite-type phosphosulfide having the composition Li(6-x)PS(5-x)Br(1+x) and to an all-solid-state battery comprising the same. A cubic garnet of the Li7La3Zr2O12 type sintered to high relative density may be used as a counterpart layer. A mixed-halogen argyrodite-type phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An all-solid-state battery comprising the LGPS and Li3PS4 material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The solid electrolyte may comprise Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4. The iodine occupies the 4a site of the cubic F-43m lattice while the bromine occupies the 4d site, which widens the lithium diffusion pathway. An ionic conductivity of 4.5 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 0.2 to 0.65. A lithium metal anode can be used as the negative electrode because the reduction stability of the solid electrolyte is improved. The solid electrolyte provides improved cycle life and ionic conductivity compared with a single-halogen argyrodite-type of the same halogen content.

title: Argyrodite-type sulfide ceramic ion conductor with mixed chlorine-bromine substitution
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor for a solid-state battery has an argyrodite-type crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Cl(x)Br(y). A niobate-coated positive electrode active material may be included in the electrode mixture. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The ceramic ion conductor is applied as the electrolyte of a solid-state battery whose positive electrode layer comprises a layered lithium transition metal oxide. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiCl relative to the argyrodite-type phase is 0.12 or less. The site occupancy of bromine on the 4a site, refined by Rietveld analysis, is 60% or more. When fired at 500 degrees C to 600 degrees C, the material shows a conductivity of 6.4 mS/cm or more and a lithium ion transference number close to unity. A solid-state battery using the ceramic ion conductor in the positive electrode layer shows improved rate capability and moisture stability.
