title: Densified garnet oxide ion-conductive solid and lithium battery including the same
abstract: A lanthanum zirconium garnet ion-conductive solid doped with aluminum and sintered with Al2O3 is described. A lithium secondary battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved ionic conductivity. The glassy matrix of a vitreous sulfide improves the contact between particles during pressing. The grain size is 4 micrometers to 30 micrometers and the relative density is 91% or more after sintering at 1070 degrees C to 1220 degrees C. A sintering aid comprising Al2O3 is added in an amount of 0.5 wt% to 5 wt% and forms a liquid phase that wets the garnet grains during sintering. Specific examples are lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3) and Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO). Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The sintered garnet is useful as a dense separator against a lithium metal negative electrode, with improved ionic conductivity and high-voltage stability.

title: Self-supporting ion-conductive solid sheet having low porosity and method for calendering the same
abstract: A free-standing ion-conductive solid sheet comprises ion-conductive solid particles and a fibrillated polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) binder forming a three-dimensional fibril network that binds the particles without a solvent. The sheet has a thickness of 30 micrometers, a porosity of 10%, a tensile strength of 3 MPa, and an ionic conductivity of 1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The sheet is calendered to a thickness of 12 micrometers to 60 micrometers and laminated onto an electrode by roll-pressing without a drying step. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is chemically compatible with a lithium metal anode and suppresses the growth of lithium filaments. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The material comprises Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, beta-Li3PS4, and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the sheet is self-supporting and can be wound on a core having a diameter of 50 mm. The Li6PS5Cl, Li3PS4, and LLZO material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. The method shortens the process and improves the ionic conductivity and cycle life of the layer.

title: Germanium-substituted Li2ZrO3-modified LLZO ceramic ion conductor stable above 5.2 V and lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ceramic ion conductor having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. An all-solid-state battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and a ceramic ion conductor layer disposed therebetween is also provided. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 1 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5.2 V. The positive electrode active material is LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4, which is charged to 4.6 V or more against the oxide ceramic ion conductor. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The viscosity of the slurry is adjusted for doctor blade coating on a PET film. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the all-solid-state battery. The oxide ceramic ion conductor enables the use of a 5 V class cathode and improves the cycle life.

title: Lithium phosphorus oxynitride protective layer for lithium metal negative electrode and lithium battery
abstract: A method for forming a protective layer on lithium metal by sputtering followed by solution coating of a polymer is described. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the ion-conductive solid layer of the solid-state lithium battery. The raw materials of the ion-conductive solid are mixed by ball milling for 4 hours to 40 hours before heat treatment. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. The material retains its conductivity after being shaped into a film by a dry process at room temperature. The material comprises Li3YCl6, and the protective layer forms an artificial interphase that is lithiophilic. The material may be used together with a halogen-substituted Li6PS5X having an impurity-free X-ray pattern. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6. The protective layer thickness is 80 nm to 400 nm and the Coulombic efficiency is 97.8% or more. The protective layer suppresses the growth of lithium dendrites and improves the cycle life of the lithium metal battery.

title: Mixed-halide ceramic ion conductor of indium and titanium and oxidation-stable lithium battery
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a lithium metal halide of the Li3MX6 type with a close-packed chloride anion sublattice and to a battery using the same. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. The halide ceramic ion conductor has an ionic conductivity of 2.1 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an oxidation stability limit of 4.2 V versus Li/Li+. The ceramic ion conductor may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The ceramic ion conductor may comprise Li7P3S11, beta-Li3PS4, and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl. A titanium-containing oxide whose reduction is suppressed may be combined with the material. The trigonal phase is obtained by heat treatment at 300 degrees C, and the monoclinic polymorph is 5% or less. The halide ceramic ion conductor is stable in contact with a layered oxide cathode without a coating, improving the ionic conductivity and electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Disclosed is a crystallized sulfide glass in which a thio-LISICON phase is precipitated from a vitreous Li2S-P2S5 matrix containing LiI. A garnet pellet with a grain size of a few micrometers and low grain boundary resistance is compatible with the material. The glass phase contains LiI in an amount of 2.5 mol% to 10 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the thio-LISICON phase. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 5.5 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. A trigonal or monoclinic halide of indium or scandium may be added to the positive electrode mixture. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the all-solid-state battery. In an all-solid-state battery the ceramic ion conductor forms the electrolyte layer and improves the cycle life. The material comprises Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS) and beta-Li3PS4 in which the glassy matrix fills the gaps between the precipitated crystals. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous LiTaO3 shell with high coverage and production method thereof
abstract: A positive electrode active material having a coating layer with a coverage of 90% or more and an average thickness of 3.2 nm to 16 nm is provided. The average thickness of the coating is 3.2 nm to 16 nm, the coverage is 90% or more, and the heat treatment temperature is 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C. The solvent is removed under vacuum so that the residual solvent is below 0.5 wt%. A silver or indium additive at the negative electrode interface is one option for dendrite suppression. Suitable compositions include Li3InCl6, lithium niobate (LiNbO3), and argyrodite Li6PS5Cl. Because no solvent is used, a dry process is applicable to the formation of the layer from the obtained powder. In an all-solid-state battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium tantalate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The tumbling fluidized bed gives uniform coating and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: Provided is a solid electrolyte comprising a vitreous matrix and a metastable Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal crystal phase, the material having a degree of crystallinity of 60%. The glass ceramic shows a lower grain boundary resistance than a fully crystalline solid electrolyte powder. The glass phase contains GeS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the Li10GeP2S12-type tetragonal phase. Li2S and P2S5 in the glass are in a molar ratio of 72:28, and the precipitated crystal phase is metastable at room temperature. The crystallized glass has an ionic conductivity of 1.2 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and a degree of crystallinity of 60%. Examples of the ion conductor include beta-Li3PS4 and Li10GeP2S12 (LGPS). In a lithium secondary battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the moisture stability. A high-voltage stable phosphate oxide may form part of the positive electrode mixture. The material is useful as a separator layer or as a conductive component of an electrode, with improved moisture stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ceramic ion conductor and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: A sulfide ceramic ion conductor having a hygroscopicity of 1 wt% or less and a tin-rich surface region is described. The ceramic ion conductor shows an ionic conductivity of 1.5 mS/cm at 25 degrees C and an H2S generation of 2 cm3/g after exposure to air having a dew point of -30 degrees C. A mixed-halide chloride-bromide conductor may be combined with the material. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The active material is preferably coated by an alkoxide route before mixing with the material. The dew point of the handling atmosphere is -30 degrees C and the exposure time is 6 hours. Specific examples are Li7P3S11 and argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The material transports lithium between the positive electrode and the negative electrode of the solid-state battery. The reduced water vapor reaction lowers the interfacial resistance and improves the sinterability.

title: Oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid and high-voltage lithium battery
abstract: Disclosed is an oxidation-resistant oxide ion-conductive solid having a widened electrochemical window for use with a high-voltage positive electrode such as LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4. An all-solid-state lithium battery using the ion-conductive solid shows stable operation at 25 degrees C and 60 degrees C with improved high-voltage stability. Specific examples are Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The powder has a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and shows an oxidation potential of 5 V. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. An LLZO garnet sintered with a lithium borate aid is one example of a dense oxide layer. The disclosure also provides a dry process for laminating the ion-conductive solid layer onto an electrode of the all-solid-state lithium battery without a drying step. The material comprises Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP), Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and the decomposition current density at 5 V is 40 microamperes per square centimeter or less. The suppression of anodic decomposition results in a stable interface and improved high-voltage stability.

title: Moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and method for handling in a dry room
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a moisture-stable sulfide ion-conductive solid and to a method of handling it in a dry room. The sulfide component may be prepared by a liquid-phase route in tetrahydrofuran or acetonitrile. The ion-conductive solid can be used as an interlayer that prevents direct contact between the sulfide layer and the electrode of the lithium secondary battery. The disclosure is applicable to Li7P3S11. The Li7P3S11 composition can be prepared as a glass ceramic by heat treatment of the glassy precursor. An H2S generation of 20 cm3/g or less and a conductivity retention of 75% or more are obtained. The cumulative H2S generation after 60 minutes of exposure to air with a dew point of -30 degrees C is 10 cm3/g. A germanium-free glass of the Li2S-P2S5 system may be used as a binder-like deformable phase. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved grain boundary resistance and sinterability.

title: Oxide ion-conductive solid with widened electrochemical window for high-voltage cathodes and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: This disclosure concerns a high-voltage stable oxide ion conductor based on phosphate-based NASICON and a method for forming its oxidation-resistant surface. The anodic decomposition product layer after 100 cycles is 10 nm or less and the capacity retention is 80%. An interlayer having a thickness of 1 micrometer to 5 micrometers may be disposed between the layer and the negative electrode. The substituted phase has a NASICON or perovskite framework in which the phosphate or titanate units are oxidation-resistant. A solution-based process with stirring and filtration may be used to obtain the sulfide precursor. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery comprising the ion-conductive solid and a lithium metal anode pressed at 2 MPa to 10 MPa. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the high-voltage stability. The layer may be formed by casting a slurry in a nonpolar solvent such as xylene with a rubber binder. The ion-conductive solid is preferably Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO) and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). An oxidation-resistant surface region comprising lithium phosphate is formed on the particles by an oxygen anneal after sintering. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved high-voltage stability.

title: Coated cathode particles having an amorphous Li3InCl6 shell with high coverage and method for preparing the same
abstract: A positive electrode active material for a battery comprising a sulfide solid electrolyte includes core particles of a layered lithium nickel transition metal oxide and a coating layer of amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) disposed on the surface of the core particles. The coated particles are heat-treated at 400 degrees C to 500 degrees C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere so that the shell remains amorphous. The powder is handled in a dry room with a dew point of -40 degrees C or lower. The coating layer comprises amorphous lithium indium chloride (Li3InCl6) and has an average thickness of 6 nm to 30 nm and a coverage of 85% or more determined by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. A dry process is preferred for forming the solid electrolyte sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. In an embodiment a halide coating containing indium chloride is applied to the active material before mixing. The thickness of the interlayer is set to 50 nm to 2 micrometers so that the resistance increase is small. Nickel accounts for 90 mol% of the transition metals, and the heat treatment is performed at 450 degrees C. The suppression of the space-charge layer results in a smaller interfacial resistance and improved electrochemical window.

title: Lithium metal negative electrode having an artificial interphase formed by solution casting and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a lithiophilic protective layer that improves the wettability of lithium and prevents direct contact between metallic lithium and the sulfide layer. A dry process in which the ceramic ion conductor powder is kneaded with a fibrillated binder is used to form the layer of the all-solid-state battery. Suitable compositions include beta-Li3PS4 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The inorganic layer comprises lithium fluoride or lithium phosphorus oxynitride and has a thickness of 300 nm. The disclosure further provides an all-solid-state battery in which at least one of the positive electrode layer and the separator layer comprises the Li3PS4 and LLZO material. The number of cycles without short circuit at 0.5 mA/cm2 is 250 cycles or more and the thickness of the polymer layer is 0.25 micrometers to 1.5 micrometers. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The inorganic layer suppresses the penetration of lithium filaments, while the polymer layer absorbs the cracks caused by volume change of the negative electrode. The bilayer structure improves the interfacial resistance compared with a single inorganic layer.

title: Densified garnet oxide solid electrolyte and lithium battery including the same
abstract: Provided is a cubic garnet oxide of the LLZO type in which the dopant tantalum stabilizes the cubic phase and the sintering aid promotes densification. In an embodiment the material is Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). The green pellet is covered with the mother powder during sintering at 1120 degrees C to 1270 degrees C, which compensates lithium volatilization. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. A metal halide synthesized by a water-mediated route can be mixed with the material. A solid-state battery comprising the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LLZO material and a method for manufacturing the same are also provided. When v is 0.4, the cubic phase fraction is 97% or more and the conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. The densification improves the mechanical strength and the grain boundary resistance of the garnet layer.

title: Solid oxide fuel cell with a barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode and a diffusion barrier layer of doped ceria
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a planar solid oxide fuel cell stack comprising unit cells with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte, metal interconnects, and a glass sealant. Because the barrier layer prevents interfacial reaction with the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode, the degradation rate is reduced to 1% per 1000 hours. The area specific resistance of the cell is 0.3 ohm cm2 or less at 650 to 800 degrees C. Hydrogen or reformed natural gas is supplied to the anode and air is supplied to the barium strontium cobalt ferrite cathode at 650 to 800 degrees C. The reversible cell with a lanthanum strontium gallate magnesite electrolyte improves the round trip efficiency of hydrogen production and power generation. The cathode comprises barium strontium cobalt ferrite and is sintered at 1000 to 1100 degrees C after the electrolyte is densified.

title: Method for producing a sulfide ceramic ion conductor through a solvate complex precipitate
abstract: This disclosure concerns the synthesis of a sulfide ion conductor through dissolution and precipitation in a nonaqueous solvent. In an embodiment the material is Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4. A protective layer of LiPON or lithium fluoride may be formed on the lithium metal by sputtering. A sheet with a fibrillated binder and low porosity can be wound on a roll. The reaction at 45 degrees C to 80 degrees C for 24 hours gives a precipitate yield of 95% or more. The solvate complex precipitate is separated by filtration and the solvent is removed at 110 degrees C to 190 degrees C under reduced pressure. The material comprises Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO) and beta-Li3PS4, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. The LLZO and Li3PS4 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in a solid-state lithium battery. A lithium-ion conductive glass ceramic may be mixed with the ceramic ion conductor in the solid-state lithium battery. The synthesized powder is made into a self-supporting film by solvent-free rolling, and the film has a porosity of 10% or less. The solvate route lowers the processing temperature and improves the grain boundary resistance of the product.

title: Ion-conductive solid slurry with controlled viscosity and solid content for doctor blade casting
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a slurry composition with controlled viscosity and solid content for forming an ion-conductive solid layer. The slurry has a solid content of 50 wt% to 70 wt% and a viscosity of 1000 mPa s to 4000 mPa s at 25 degrees C, which is suitable for doctor blade casting. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. An oxide stable up to 5 V versus Li/Li+ can be used on the positive electrode side. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the ion-conductive solid layer. The viscosity of 2000 mPa s allows a uniform wet film, and the dried thickness variation is 5% or less. The wet film is dried at 120 degrees C and the dried layer has a thickness of 8 micrometers to 40 micrometers. The synthesis comprises reacting the raw materials in a suspension with stirring and removing the residual solvent before the sheet is formed. Lithium ions migrate through the material at 25 degrees C with a transference number close to unity. The wet process is useful for forming a layer on a large area, with improved sheet formability.

title: Lithium yttrium chloride-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery and all-solid lithium cell
abstract: Provided is a coated active material in which an amorphous Li3YCl6 layer prevents the formation of a space-charge layer at the interface with the sulfide. The core particles have an average diameter of 3 micrometers to 12 micrometers and the coverage of the shell is 80%. The all-solid-state battery may further include an interlayer between the positive electrode layer and the solid electrolyte layer. A dense garnet layer of 95% relative density can be laminated with the material. A coverage of 80% and a thickness of 8 nm give an interfacial resistance reduction of 30%. The LiNbO3 material is combined with a negative electrode of graphite, silicon, or lithium metal in an all-solid-state battery. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LiNbO3 material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. The hygroscopic behavior of the sulfide is suppressed by a Sn-substituted surface. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The coated cathode is useful in a sulfide-based positive electrode mixture, with improved interfacial resistance.

title: Oxide ceramic ion conductor having a surface region suppressing anodic decomposition and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Described is an oxide ceramic ion conductor whose decomposition current at 5 V is 20 microamperes per square centimeter or less, enabling operation with a 5 V class cathode. Specific examples are Li0.33La0.56TiO3 (LLTO), lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and Li1.3Al0.3Ti1.7(PO4)3 (LATP). An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ceramic ion conductor having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. Ball milling of the raw materials for the LLTO, Li2ZrO3, and LATP material in a sealed pot is performed prior to firing. A wet-chemical synthesis through a solvate complex precipitate gives a fine sulfide powder. The electrochemical window measured by cyclic voltammetry on a blocking electrode extends to 5.5 V versus Li/Li+. A capacity retention of 80% after 200 cycles at 4.6 V is obtained with the substituted oxide. The material is useful as a catholyte in a high-voltage positive electrode mixture, with improved grain boundary resistance and high-voltage stability.

title: Nickel-rich cathode material coated with Li2ZrO3 and method for producing the same
abstract: A core-shell positive electrode active material for a sulfide-based solid-state lithium battery is described. The solid electrolyte may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. In a solid-state lithium battery the solid electrolyte forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. Roll-pressing the powder with PTFE fibrils forms the separator layer. The core particles have a median diameter D50 of 2 micrometers and nickel content of 50 mol% or more. The core particles are secondary particles of a layered oxide in which nickel accounts for 50 mol% or more of the transition metals. The precursor may be precipitated from ethyl acetate and dried before use. The high coverage of the coating results in improved electrochemical window at a charging voltage of 4.3 V or more.

title: Sulfide ion-conductive solid resistant to hydrolysis under humid air for lithium battery
abstract: A moisture-resistant sulfide ion-conductive solid comprises a lithium phosphosulfide phase in which part of the phosphorus or sulfur is substituted by arsenic-free antimony and a surface region enriched in a soft-acid element. The powder is amorphized by mechanical milling in a dry room with a dew point of -50 degrees C or lower and then heat-treated at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C. The electrode mixture of the all-solid-state battery may include an active material provided with a halide coating instead of an oxide coating. The cell may include a lithium nucleation additive to prevent short circuit. In an embodiment the material is Li7P3S11 and Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO). Heat treatment at 450 degrees C to 550 degrees C gives a conductivity of 1 mS/cm and a retention of 90% after humid exposure. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the ion-conductive solid having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The ion-conductive solid may be a glass ceramic obtained by partially crystallizing a glass. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The material is useful for electrode slurry processing in a dry room, with improved ionic conductivity.

title: Iodine-substituted argyrodite ion-conductive solid and lithium battery and all-solid-state battery including the same
abstract: A lithium phosphosulfide ion-conductive solid having a cubic argyrodite structure and a controlled halogen occupancy is described. Calendering of the kneaded powder gives a sheet of 30 micrometers thickness. In an all-solid-state battery the ion-conductive solid forms the electrolyte layer and improves the electrochemical window. An ionic conductivity of 3.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. A lithium metal halide of the Li3YCl6 or Li3InCl6 type may be used as a catholyte on the positive electrode side. An all-solid-state battery using a lithium metal anode together with the ion-conductive solid shows stable plating and stripping for 300 cycles or more. Partial substitution of chlorine with iodine increases the anion disorder between the sulfur and halogen sites without forming a LiCl impurity phase. A mixed-halogen argyrodite phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 550 degrees C. The ion-conductive solid powder can be formed into a free-standing film by a dry process without any solvent. Compared with Li6PS5Cl, the iodine-substituted argyrodite shows a higher conductivity and better electrochemical window.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having a glassy matrix and precipitated crystal phase
abstract: A glassy sulfide solid electrolyte with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Coverage of the coating on the core particle is preferably 85% or more. The glass phase contains SiS2 in an amount of 1 mol% to 4 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. The powder has a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers and gives a pellet conductivity of 1.8 mS/cm after pressing at 360 MPa. Specific examples are Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl and beta-Li3PS4. The lithium metal negative electrode is preferably covered by a lithiophilic bilayer protective layer. When a lithium metal anode is used, the layer facing the anode preferably has a thickness of 10 micrometers or more. An all-solid-state battery containing the crystallized glass shows improved cycle life and rate performance.

title: Lithium niobate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: This disclosure concerns a coating layer of lithium niobate formed by wet coating with an alkoxide solution on nickel-rich NCM particles. The material comprises argyrodite Li6PS5Cl, Li3InCl6, and lithium zirconate (Li2ZrO3), and the coating layer is disposed between the active material and the sulfide ion conductor. The coating solution contains a lithium alkoxide and a precursor of the lithium niobate, and is applied to the core particles in a tumbling fluidized bed. The interlayer reduces the interfacial resistance of the lithium secondary battery and keeps the contact area during volume change of the electrode. An alloy-forming additive improves the Coulombic efficiency of plating and stripping. The sulfide may be substituted with tin or oxygen to improve the moisture stability and suppress hydrogen sulfide generation. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ion-conductive solid. The lithium niobate shell lowers the oxidative decomposition of the sulfide at the cathode interface, improving the cycle life and electrochemical window.

title: Wet-chemical method for producing a sulfide solid electrolyte with low residual solvent
abstract: Provided is a method in which a solvate complex of Li3PS4 is precipitated from a mixed solvent of ethanol and tetrahydrofuran, dried under vacuum, and heat-treated. The active material having a halide coating is mixed with the material in a weight ratio of 70:30 to 85:15. A residual solvent content of 0.5 wt% or less is achieved by vacuum drying, and the conductivity is 3 mS/cm. A sulfide glass ceramic can be used as the matrix of the solid electrolyte layer of the all-solid-state battery. The dissolution of P2S5 in the solvent is followed by precipitation of a complex that contains one to three solvent molecules per formula unit. The material comprises beta-Li3PS4, Li7La3Zr2O12 garnet (LLZO), and Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, which is obtained from the solution-based precursor after drying and heat treatment. An all-solid-state battery with an electrolyte layer of the solid electrolyte having a thickness of 20 micrometers to 100 micrometers and the material in the positive electrode layer is also provided. The solid electrolyte powder may be refined by ball milling to a median diameter D50 of 5 micrometers. Devitrification of the amorphous phase is controlled by the heat treatment temperature. The disclosure is applied to a lithium battery comprising the solid electrolyte. An all-solid-state battery using the solid electrolyte obtained by the method shows improved grain boundary resistance.

title: Lithium metal halide ion-conductive solid represented by Li(3-z)Er(1-z)Hf(z)Br6 and electrode mixture containing the same
abstract: Disclosed is a halide ion-conductive solid in which hafnium is substituted for part of the erbium in a lithium erbium bromide framework. The halide is synthesized by mechanochemical reaction of LiBr, ErBr3, and HfBr4 followed by heat treatment at 200 degrees C to 300 degrees C. Examples of the ion conductor include Li3YCl6, Li3InCl6, and lithium fluoride (LiF). A lithium secondary battery comprising a positive electrode layer, a negative electrode layer, and an ion-conductive solid layer disposed therebetween is also provided. A protected lithium metal negative electrode is one example of the counter electrode. A dendrite-suppressing additive such as magnesium or zinc may be placed at the lithium metal interface. The median particle diameter D50 is 0.5 micrometers and the pellet conductivity is 0.8 mS/cm after pressing at 300 MPa. The hafnium substitution lowers the raw material cost of the rare earth halide and improves the electrochemical window.

title: Lithium tungstate-coated positive electrode active material for sulfide-based solid-state battery for lithium battery
abstract: Described is a cathode particle coated with a nanometer-thick Li2WO4 shell that lowers the interfacial resistance. Also described is a solid-state battery comprising the ceramic ion conductor in the electrode mixture and in the electrolyte layer. The shell suppresses the space-charge layer and the diffusion of transition metals into the sulfide during charging above 4.3 V. In an embodiment the ceramic ion conductor layer comprises a glass ceramic having a crystallinity of 50% to 90%. A styrene-butadiene rubber binder dissolved in a nonpolar solvent may be used for the wet film. A moisture-resistant sulfide with low hydrolysis is one example of the conductor. Examples of the ion conductor include argyrodite-type Li6PS5Cl. The coated active material shows a capacity retention of 90% or more after 100 cycles with a sulfide ceramic ion conductor. A lithium cell comprising the material in at least one layer is also described. A solid-state battery using the coated active material shows improved electrochemical window and high-voltage stability and rate capability.

title: Crystallized sulfide glass ion-conductive solid containing a beta-Li3PS4 phase and method for preparing the same
abstract: A glassy sulfide ion-conductive solid with a precipitated crystal phase and a method for its heat treatment are provided. Lithium filament penetration along grain boundaries is suppressed when the current density is below the critical value. Atomic layer deposition of a thin nitride or oxide protective layer on the lithium metal is one option. The glass transition temperature is 200 degrees C, the crystallization onset is 300 degrees C, and the conductivity reaches 1.8 mS/cm. A dry process is preferred for forming the ion-conductive solid sheet because contact with a polar solvent is avoided. The glass phase contains Li2O in an amount of 4 mol% to 16 mol%, which lowers the crystallization temperature and stabilizes the beta-Li3PS4 phase. Examples of the ion conductor include Li7P3S11, Li6PS5X Li6PS5Cl, and beta-Li3PS4. Precipitation of the metastable phase gives a conductivity higher than that of the glass, while the ionic conductivity is retained.

title: Sulfide solid electrolyte having Li6PS5X structure with controlled halogen occupancy and lithium battery
abstract: A sulfide solid electrolyte for a solid-state battery has a Li6PS5X crystal structure and a composition represented by Li(7-a)PS(6-a)Br(x)I(y). The LGPS and Li6PS5Cl material is used in a solid-state battery together with a positive electrode active material and a negative electrode. A mixed-halogen Li6PS5X phase with a lattice parameter of 9.85 angstroms to 9.95 angstroms is obtained by firing at 450 degrees C. An ionic conductivity of 7.2 mS/cm or more at 25 degrees C is obtained when x satisfies 1.1 to 1.5. The positive electrode active material may be coated with lithium niobate or a similar oxide to lower the interfacial resistance. In a X-ray diffraction pattern measured using CuK-alpha radiation, the peak intensity ratio attributed to LiBr relative to the Li6PS5X phase is 0.075 or less. The glass ceramic phase improves the contact between solid electrolyte particles during pressing. A silver-containing protective layer on the lithium metal improves the deposition uniformity. The suppression of the impurity phase results in a smaller interfacial resistance and better electrochemical window.
